owner.description: Person or team accountable for the capability: its roadmap, budget and risk decisions. Set it on a domain or group and everything beneath inherits it unless it sets its own. Name a User or Team entity by its name, id or (for a User) email.

criticality.description: How much the business suffers when this capability is unavailable or degraded. It sets recovery targets and how closely the capability is reviewed.

x-enumDescriptions.low: Can be down for days using workarounds, with little customer or financial impact.
x-enumDescriptions.medium: Disruption hurts within a day, causing delays and manual workarounds but limited customer impact.
x-enumDescriptions.high: An outage stops core operations or causes financial, legal or customer harm within hours. Needs a recovery plan, tested failover and named on-call support.

review_cycle_days.description: Days between scheduled reviews of the capability's owner, providers and maturity.

maturity.description: How well established the way of delivering this capability is.

x-enumDescriptions.initial: Ad hoc; it depends on individuals and has no documented process.
x-enumDescriptions.pilot: Being trialled in part of the organisation.

lifecycle.description: Where the capability is in its life.

x-enumDescriptions.retire: Being phased out. Nothing active may sit beneath it.

Asset.description: Anything the business runs or owns that can provide or need capabilities.

owner.description: Team or person accountable for running the asset. Name a User or Team by its name, id or (for a User) email.

lifecycle.description: Where the asset is in its life.

x-enumDescriptions.plan: Planned or being built; it doesn't provide anything yet.
x-enumDescriptions.retire: Being decommissioned. It no longer counts as a provider of capabilities.

Application.description: A software product, bought or built.

vendor.description: Supplier of the product, or "internal" for software built in-house.

Service.description: A shared technical service that other systems rely on.

Team.description: A group of people that delivers or needs capabilities.

head.description: Person who leads the team. Name a User by its name, id or email.

lifecycle.description: Whether the team exists yet, is working, or is being wound down.

x-enumDescriptions.retire: Being wound down. It no longer counts as a provider of capabilities.

User.description: A person with an identity in the organisation's systems.

email.description: Primary email address, used as the person's sign-in and contact address. It is a key: unique across users, and a reference to a User may use it instead of the name.

lifecycle.description: Where the person's account is in its life.

x-enumDescriptions.plan: Being onboarded; the account is not in use yet.

Link_exposes.description: The entity delivers this capability for the rest of the organisation.

coverage.description: How much of the capability this entity delivers.

x-enumDescriptions.partial: Delivers only part of it; another provider is needed for the rest.

Link_requires.description: The entity needs this capability to do its job. Something active must expose it.

dependency.description: What happens to the entity when nothing provides the capability.

x-enumDescriptions.hard: It cannot operate. An unmet hard requirement is a break.
x-enumDescriptions.soft: It keeps running in a degraded way.

Link_depends_on.description: The application calls or relies on another application or service at runtime.

criticality.description: How badly the application suffers when the dependency fails.

x-enumDescriptions.low: Hardly noticed, or easily worked around.
x-enumDescriptions.medium: Some features fail; the rest keeps working.
